bull.b: Rapid DTC growth strengthens On’s control over pricing, customer relationships, and brand presentation while improving channel mix. A larger owned retail and e-commerce base can support durable margin quality and reduce reliance on wholesale partners as the company scales.

The combination of a 65%+ gross margin and roughly 20% adjusted EBITDA margin indicates meaningful operating leverage and premium brand positioning. Sustained profitability gives On resources to fund product innovation, geographic expansion, and customer acquisition without sacrificing financial resilience.

Strong APAC growth and rapid expansion in apparel and training demonstrate that On is extending beyond a single footwear category and its established markets. Broader participation across regions and products can diversify revenue sources and increase customer lifetime value over time.

bear.b: Wholesale momentum is materially weaker than On’s DTC performance, particularly in the Americas, where products are selling below ambitions in a promotional marketplace. Persistent channel weakness could constrain sales cadence and make growth more dependent on the company’s own retail execution.

A sizeable inventory increase creates an execution requirement as management calibrates wholesale sell-in and works through channel conditions. If inventory growth remains ahead of demand, On could face slower cash conversion or greater promotional pressure, even though management cited volume and FX as the main drivers.

Higher U.S. import tariffs can pressure product economics and cash flows in a key market, while the timing of potential refunds remains uncertain. Because management excluded those benefits from guidance, the business must deliver its outlook without relying on an unconfirmed offset to tariff costs.
